treasury_auctions.narrative: The Sep 15 20Y reopening (912810UX4) shows a materially weaker demand mix than the trailing 20 comparable auctions: dealers absorbed 16.7% of the issue (vs a ~10.8% trailing average, 100th percentile -- the highest dealer take-down in the bucket), while indirect (foreign/institutional) demand fell to 52.1% (vs a ~60.4% trailing average, 5th percentile). Bid-to-cover at 2.57 was only mildly soft (35th percentile, close to the 2.64 trailing average), and the high yield (5.42%) cleared without a meaningful tail relative to when-issued expectations. This reads as an isolated demand-composition wobble -- a "duration repricing" event with dealers absorbing more of the reopening -- rather than confirmed "Treasury intermediation stress": there is no corroborating repo-spread widening or dealer-inventory build evidence available this run, and nominal yields barely moved (US10Y +0.2bp, US30Y +1.7bp on the day). Per methodology this single print is not sufficient to downgrade the state from Healthy; the next test (91282CRE3, a 9Y10M Note reopening, Sep 17) will be the confirming or disconfirming data point.
